title: Unveiling a hidden threat: whole genome sequencing exposes the cross-hospital spread of extensively drug-resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa
author: Edwin Kamau
license_note: figshare article detail endpoint license.name: CC BY 4.0

steps.title: Collect patient specimens
steps.instruction: Obtain clinical samples from patients according to standard clinical protocols, yielding 10 extensively drug‑resistant Pseudomonas aeruginosa ST235 isolates (2 from the index patient, 4 from a secondary patient, and 4 from the index patient’s ICU sink collected 9 months later).

steps.title: Swab ICU sink drains
steps.instruction: Swab the sink drains in ICU rooms that were previously occupied by the study patients to assess environmental contamination.

steps.title: Culture swab samples
steps.instruction: Inoculate the swab material onto Brain‑Heart Infusion (BHI) agar and Blood Agar Plate (BAP) media and incubate under appropriate conditions to recover bacterial growth.

steps.title: PCR screen isolates
steps.instruction: Perform PCR on cultured isolates using primers targeting the 16S rRNA gene and the Pseudomonas aeruginosa ecfX gene to confirm species identity.

steps.title: Whole genome sequence isolates
steps.instruction: Extract DNA from each of the 10 XDR P. aeruginosa ST235 isolates and conduct whole‑genome sequencing (WGS) using the laboratory’s standard sequencing platform.

steps.title: Assess genetic relatedness
steps.instruction: Analyze the WGS data with core‑genome multilocus sequence typing (cgMLST) and single‑nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) analysis to determine relatedness among isolates.

steps.title: Identify resistance genes
steps.instruction: Run AMRFinderPlus on the assembled genomes to detect antimicrobial‑resistance genes, including blaVIM‑2.

steps.title: Perform phylogenetic comparison
steps.instruction: Compare the isolates to publicly available genomes from NCBI and the MRSN database to generate a global phylogeny and assess clustering with international ST235 strains.
